title: Quarterly orchestration: alignment cadence and decision radar for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective:
Create a single quarterly orchestration framework (cadence + decision radar) that the Hosted API and Model Catalog teams use for committing and defending roadmap items. The framework should reduce ad-hoc prioritization meetings, make trade-offs explicit (capacity vs. quality vs. SLAs), and provide a repeatable canary/rollback schedule for model rotations and hosted endpoint changes.

Scope:
- Align cross-functional stakeholders (Product, Eng runtime, Infra, DX, Research) on a single commitment calendar for Q1 2026 items affecting hosted endpoints and model catalog tiering.
- Define a 'decision radar' document and cadence that surfaces critical gating signals (capacity forecasts, regression evals, SLA risk, security/compliance blockers).
- Produce a staged rollout template (canary windows, traffic hedges, fallback variants) for model swaps and hosted API feature flags.
- Tie runway commitments to measurable success metrics (latency P50/P95, unit token cost, eval pass rates) and to OKR swimlanes.

Deliverables:
1) Decision Radar template (Confluence) with clear signal thresholds and owners.
2) Quarterly Commitment Calendar (shared Google Sheet + Console dashboard view) with canary windows and staffing expectations.
3) Rollout template + checklist (PRD + ops runbook) for model variant promotion and hosted endpoint changes.
4) Metrics dashboard spec for the Console to show commit health prior to and during canary.

Acceptance criteria:
- Template reviewed and approved by Eng runtime lead, Head of Research, and Security.
- Two pilot commitments scheduled on the calendar for December and January (one model rotation, one hosted-feature toggle).
- Dashboard spec accepted by Console PM and assigned to a sprint in Cycle 2026-W03.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Capacity estimates may change after commitments. Mitigation: reserve a 20% burst hedge and require capacity sign-off 10 business days before canary.
- Risk: Regression evals fail during canary. Mitigation: automatic rollback policy with pre-defined fallback variants and communication runbook.
- Risk: Too many stakeholders -> slow decisions. Mitigation: weekly 30-min decision sync with explicit RACI and emergency escalation path.

Timeline (high level):
- Week 1 (Nov 15–21): Draft decision radar + stakeholder review.
- Week 2 (Nov 22–28): Iterate templates, finalize calendar slots, identify pilots.
- Week 3 (Dec 1–7): Run pilot #1 (model rotation) and capture learnings.
- Week 4 (Dec 8–14): Update templates & dashboard spec; schedule pilot #2.
